name: Giant Cell Tumor of Bone

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Giant Cell Tumor of Bone

criteria.description: Presence of numerous multinucleated osteoclast-like giant cells uniformly distributed among mononuclear stromal cells
Lytic, eccentric, and expansile lesion typically located in the epiphysis of long bones on imaging
Localized pain and swelling at the affected site with possible joint dysfunction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of multinucleated giant cells with characteristic radiological findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires correlation of clinical, radiological, and histopathological data to exclude other giant cell-rich lesions.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Localized bone swelling with palpable mass

searchTerms: bone area with bone loss on x-ray

common.symptomName: Joint stiffness adjacent to tumor site
Reduced range of motion in affected limb
searchTerms: difficulty moving affected arm or leg

occasional.symptomName: Soft tissue swelling surrounding bone lesion
searchTerms: swelling of soft tissue around bone lesion
soft tissue mass near bone tumor

occasional.symptomName: Mild constitutional symptoms such as low-grade fever
searchTerms: mild general symptoms like low-grade fever

occasional.symptomName: Nerve compression symptoms due to tumor expansion
searchTerms: tingling or numbness due to tumor

rare.symptomName: Pulmonary metastases presenting with respiratory symptoms
Malignant transformation with aggressive local invasion

searchTerms: elevated calcium levels caused by cancer

laboratory: Normal or mildly elevated serum calcium
imaging: Radiographs showing eccentric, lytic, expansile epiphyseal lesion with non-sclerotic margins
MRI demonstrating soft tissue extension and cystic areas
CT scan for surgical planning and detection of cortical breach
genetic: H3F3A gene mutations identified in majority of cases
other: Histopathology revealing multinucleated osteoclast-like giant cells and mononuclear stromal cells

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of blood-filled cystic spaces on imaging
Lack of uniform distribution of giant cells histologically
Presence of chondroid matrix on histology
Smaller lesion size and less aggressive behavior
Associated with elevated parathyroid hormone and hypercalcemia
Clinical and biochemical evidence of hyperparathyroidism

redFlags: Rapidly increasing size of bone lesion
references: World Health Organization Classification of Tumors of Soft Tissue and Bone, 5th Edition, 2020
Dorfman HD, Czerniak B. Bone Cancers. Cancer. 1995;75(1 Suppl):203-210.
